name: TVHeadend EX
description: TVHeadend EX is an independent, unofficial TVHeadend integration for Jellyfin. It began as a fork of jellyfin/jellyfin-plugin-tvheadend and has since been developed separately, with its own playback architecture and its own plugin identity. Alpha: expect breakage, and read the changelog before installing.
overview: Live TV and recordings from TVHeadend -- an independent plugin, alpha builds

versions.changelog:
A new plugin, and a tidier shelf of recordings.

This is the first release under the name TVHeadend EX. It is a separate plugin now rather than a
replacement for the official one, which means Jellyfin cannot update you into it: uninstall the
old TVHeadend plugin, then install this one. Your settings are waiting for you on the other side.

Recordings play in the Android app again. It was asking the server for a recording under a name
the server had never heard of, getting an answer with nothing in it, and showing you a black
screen without a word of explanation. It now asks under the name Jellyfin itself gave the
recording.

And they bring their sound with them. A recording's audio tracks now arrive labelled the way a
live channel's always were, so your client can tell the German soundtrack from the audio
description and pick one it can actually decode -- instead of starting, playing nothing, and
stopping a second later.

Recordings from the stubborn channels play too. A few broadcasters, Das Erste among them, never
send the kind of frame Android's decoder refuses to start without, so their recordings were a
spinner that never resolved. Those are now re-encoded on the way out -- but only those, and only
for the clients that need it. Everything else, on every other device, is still handed to you
exactly as TVHeadend stored it.

Recordings finally sort themselves out. Movies, Sports, News and Kids were empty folders in every
version so far, because the plugin was reading what a recording is and then throwing it away. It
no longer does, so a film lands with the films.

Radio recordings are radio. They were being published as video, which is a lot of black screen
for a concert.

Recordings are as long as they are. A recording you stopped early was still being listed at the
length it was booked for, so the progress bar promised minutes that were never written and
seeking into them found nothing. The length now comes from the file itself. One that is still
recording no longer claims a finished length at all, which is what it is.

Series recordings know what a series is. A new one is tied to the link TVHeadend itself uses to
connect the episodes, so it follows the programme rather than hunting for its title — and a
title with a full stop or a bracket in it no longer quietly matches half the schedule. Rules you
already had are read properly at last: the right days, the right time of day on the server's own
clock, and the settings TVHeadend has that Jellyfin cannot show are left alone instead of being
wiped every time you edit one.

Artwork that arrives after a recording is scheduled now actually reaches it, instead of being
quietly dropped every time.

And the list of recordings no longer goes stale. After a restart Jellyfin could serve you the
previous run's recordings for hours; it now notices the moment TVHeadend changes something.
